readout_other: LFP of PVT and PFC; EMG-defined loss and recovery of consciousness (duration of anesthesia)
direction_notes: TUS of the PVT shortened propofol-anaesthesia duration (TUS1 19.86 min, TUS2 17.86 min vs sham 33.14 min) and increased [60-100 Hz] LFP power in PVT and PFC.

exposures.label: TUS to paraventricular thalamus (before or after propofol)

timing.protocol_description: Fundamental frequency 500 kHz, PRF 1 Hz, duty cycle 5% and stimulation duration 50 ms; total stimulation time 20 min per mouse. TUS1 was given before anaesthesia and TUS2 once loss of consciousness was confirmed.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Mice were randomly assigned into three groups: the Sham group (mice were not administered TUS, $n = 7 )$ , the TUS1 group (mice were administered TUS prior to anesthesia, $n = 7 )$ and TUS2 group (mice were administered TUS after entering anesthesia, n = 7).

flags.reason: Paper lists a 'stimulation duration' of 50 ms; with PRF 1 Hz and DC 5% this is the pulse duration (resolved by arithmetic, burst rule).
Recorded as total stimulation time per mouse (20 min = 1200 s), as the paper gives no other train length.
21 mice in three groups of 7; exposed groups are TUS1 and TUS2 (7 each); total exposed not stated.
Pressure 0.51 MPa 'at these parameters'; domain not stated; peak vs RMS not stated.
TUS1 delivered before signal acquisition; TUS2 during anaesthesia with recording; timing relative to sonication not explicit.
PVT is paraventricular thalamus; mapped to thalamus. Electrode coordinates given; TUS aimed with a collimator.
